api_v1.title: BXTI Add-on for Proofpoint SER
api_v1.license_name: Splunk End User License for Third Party Content
api_v1.description:
BXTI Add-on for Proofpoint SER brings Proofpoint Secure Email Relay (SER) usage and delivery-failure reporting into Splunk through native, read-only API collection. It helps administrators monitor reported message volumes, throughput and delivery failures without a separate automation platform.

Choose from eight overview and summary report types, including message usage, throughput, relay-user and tag reports, and message-failure summaries. Configure API credentials, destination index, polling interval, initial backfill and sourcetype directly in the add-on.

Optional domain and recipient failure breakdowns are disabled by default and can be enabled for relay-user or tag failure inputs. Daily collection supports checkpointed catch-up and suppression of unchanged report rows.

This add-on collects reporting aggregates, not individual email messages or message content. It is specific to Proofpoint SER, not Proofpoint TAP, Essentials or other Proofpoint APIs. It does not include dashboards or alert rules and does not claim CIM data-model compliance.
api_v1.documentation:
Collection capabilities

The add-on provides eight selectable report types with these default sourcetypes:

  • Usage overview: proofpoint:ser:usage:overview
  • Message usage: proofpoint:ser:usage:messages
  • Throughput: proofpoint:ser:usage:throughput
  • Relay-user usage: proofpoint:ser:usage:relay:users
  • Tag usage: proofpoint:ser:usage:tags
  • Message failures: proofpoint:ser:failure:messages
  • Relay-user failures: proofpoint:ser:failure:relay:users
  • Tag failures: proofpoint:ser:failure:tags

Create one input per account and report type. Each input has a configurable destination index, polling interval and prefilled, editable sourcetype. Credentials are held in Splunk's encrypted credential storage and are not included in the distributed package.

Optional detailed failure reports

For relay-user and tag failure inputs, enable Include detailed failure reports to collect associated domain and recipient failure breakdowns. This option is unchecked by default. Detail events use the selected summary sourcetype with :domain or :recipient appended and are written to the same index.

Recipient reports can contain email addresses. Enable them only where your data-handling and index-access policies permit. Detail and summary reports can overlap; do not add their totals together.

Timing and backfill

Daily reports are requested one date at a time using completed UTC days. Initial backfill choices are No backfill, 7 days, 14 days or 30 days. No backfill begins with the first completed UTC day after the input starts. This is a collection scheduling convention, not a guarantee of the vendor's reporting timezone or data-finalization time.

The initial starting date is checkpointed. Changing the backfill selection later does not rewind an existing input. Catch-up resumes across polls when configured page or day limits are reached. The default reconciliation window rechecks the last three eligible completed days for corrections, suppressing unchanged rows.

Usage overview is a current license-period snapshot; daily backfill and reconciliation settings do not apply to it. Event output is at-least-once, so recovery from a failure can replay records. Use the most recent observation for each stable record key when calculating aggregate totals.

Search and scope

Set the proofpoint_ser_index search macro to your destination index expression. The proofpoint_ser_events macro selects the standard SER sourcetypes. If you override sourcetypes, also update the search filter and supply equivalent JSON field-extraction settings.

This release is for SER reporting aggregates, not individual email-message events or message content. It includes no dashboards, alert rules or automatic notifications. No CIM data-model compliance is claimed. It does not configure or change Proofpoint relay users, domains, connectors, tags or suppression settings.

Live local validation covered daily throughput and message-usage collection, plus successful empty relay-user responses. Other report types and optional details still require representative live-data validation in the destination environment. The package README documents additional limitations and operational considerations.

api_v1.title: UniFi Network Add-on for Splunk
api_v1.description: The UniFi Network Add-on for Splunk polls UniFi Network controllers via the Integration API v1 to collect network infrastructure inventory, telemetry, and reference data. The add-on retrieves configuration details for sites, devices, clients, networks, firewall policies, WiFi broadcasts, VPN servers, DNS policies, and hotspot vouchers. It also collects per-device performance statistics and large reference datasets such as country codes and DPI application classifications. All data is indexed into Splunk with structured source types that correspond to specific UniFi configuration objects and metrics. The add-on maps UniFi events and inventory to the Common Information Model (CIM) domains for Inventory, Network Traffic, Network Sessions, and Performance, enabling integration with Splunk Enterprise Security and IT Service Intelligence (ITSI). Dashboards provide visibility into client activity, network health, and device performance. API credentials are stored encrypted, and the add-on operates in read-only mode.
api_v1.documentation:
Overview

The UniFi Network Add-on for Splunk integrates with UniFi Network controllers through the Integration API v1 endpoint (/proxy/network/integration/v1). It retrieves network infrastructure data across three polling categories: inventory, telemetry, and reference data. The add-on operates in read-only mode and stores API credentials in encrypted form.

Data Collection

The add-on provides three modular data inputs, each with a configurable polling interval:

UniFi Inventory Input

Collects configuration and inventory data at a default interval of 180 seconds. Each data type can be toggled individually and produces a dedicated source type:

  • unifi:site — Site configuration and metadata
  • unifi:device — Basic device inventory
  • unifi:device:detail — Extended device attributes
  • unifi:device:pending — Devices awaiting adoption
  • unifi:device_tag — Device tagging and classification
  • unifi:client — Connected client inventory
  • unifi:network — Network configuration summaries
  • unifi:network:detail — Detailed network settings
  • unifi:network:reference — Network reference mappings
  • unifi:firewall:zone — Firewall zone definitions
  • unifi:firewall:policy — Firewall policy configurations
  • unifi:acl_rule — Access control list rules
  • unifi:wifi:broadcast — WiFi SSID broadcast settings
  • unifi:wan — WAN interface configurations
  • unifi:vpn:server — VPN server configurations
  • unifi:vpn:tunnel — VPN tunnel definitions
  • unifi:dns:policy — DNS policy settings
  • unifi:traffic_matching_list — Traffic classification lists
  • unifi:radius:profile — RADIUS authentication profiles
  • unifi:hotspot:voucher — Guest hotspot voucher data
  • unifi:info — Controller system information

UniFi Telemetry Input

Collects per-device performance statistics and full device detail at a default interval of 60 seconds. This input generates one API call per device per enabled collector. On large fleets, the polling interval should be increased to reduce API load. Source types include:

  • unifi:device:stats — Device performance metrics (CPU, memory, uptime, throughput)
  • unifi:device:detail — Real-time device state and configuration

UniFi Reference Input

Collects large, near-static reference datasets at a default interval of 86400 seconds (24 hours). Source types include:

  • unifi:ref:country — Country code reference data
  • unifi:ref:dpi_application — Deep Packet Inspection application catalog
  • unifi:ref:dpi_category — DPI application category mappings

CIM Compliance

The add-on includes field aliases, calculated fields, and CIM tags that map UniFi data to version 3.3.0 of the Splunk Common Information Model. Supported data models include:

  • Inventory — Device and client inventory tracking
  • Network Traffic — Network flow and traffic classification
  • Network Sessions — Client session and connection data
  • Performance — Device performance and health metrics

CIM normalization enables the add-on to integrate with Splunk Enterprise Security correlation searches, notable event management, and asset/identity lookups. It also supports ITSI service health monitoring and KPI calculations.

Dashboards

Three built-in dashboards provide operational visibility:

  • UniFi - Overview — Summary of controller health, site status, and device inventory
  • UniFi - Device Health — Device performance metrics, uptime, and resource utilization
  • UniFi - Clients & Network — Client connection trends, network usage, and session analytics

Security and Authentication

The add-on authenticates to the UniFi controller using an API key generated in the controller's Settings → Control Plane → Integrations interface. API keys are stored encrypted within Splunk's credential storage subsystem and accessed via the Configuration → Accounts page in the add-on. All communication occurs over HTTPS.

Performance Considerations

On deployments with large device fleets, the Telemetry input interval should be increased from the default 60 seconds to reduce API load. The input makes one API call per device per enabled collector, so polling frequency scales linearly with device count. All inputs should be configured to send data to the same dedicated index for optimal indexing performance and simplified CIM acceleration configuration.

api_v1.title: Process-IT Add-on for Stormshield
api_v1.description:
The Stormshield Add-on provides event breaking, field extraction, and Common Information Model (CIM) compliance for Stormshield firewall syslog data within Splunk.

The add-on processes raw Stormshield syslog events and classifies them into typed sourcetypes based on log category, including filter, connection, web, authentication, system, plugin, intrusion detection, server, DHCP, VPN, FTP, POP3, SMTP, SSL, XVPN, PVM, and sandboxing events.

Each classified event is mapped to the appropriate CIM data model, enabling normalized field names and accelerated security use cases across Network Traffic, Web, Authentication, Intrusion Detection, Network Sessions, Change, and Vulnerabilities domains.

This allows direct use with Splunk Enterprise Security.

The add-on is designed for deployment on heavy forwarders or indexers that receive syslog data directly from Stormshield firewalls.
api_v1.documentation:
Overview

The Stormshield Add-on ingests syslog data from Stormshield firewalls and transforms it into structured, CIM-compliant events. The add-on performs automatic sourcetype classification, extracting the log type from each event and routing it to the corresponding stormshield:<logtype> sourcetype. This classification enables precise field extraction and CIM mapping tailored to each category of firewall activity.

Supported Event Types

The add-on recognizes and processes the following Stormshield log types:

  • stormshield:filter – Firewall filtering decisions and policy actions
  • stormshield:connection – Connection tracking and session lifecycle events
  • stormshield:web – HTTP/HTTPS traffic and URL filtering activity
  • stormshield:auth – Authentication attempts and user session management
  • stormshield:system – Firewall system events and administrative actions
  • stormshield:plugin – Plugin-specific logging
  • stormshield:ids – Intrusion detection and prevention alerts
  • stormshield:server – Server-side protocol events
  • stormshield:dhcp – DHCP lease and request activity
  • stormshield:vpn – VPN tunnel establishment and termination
  • stormshield:ftp – FTP protocol events
  • stormshield:pop3 – POP3 email retrieval events
  • stormshield:smtp – SMTP email transmission events
  • stormshield:ssl – SSL/TLS handshake and certificate events
  • stormshield:xvpn – Extended VPN logging
  • stormshield:pvm – Policy violation monitoring
  • stormshield:sandboxing – Sandboxing analysis results

CIM Data Model Coverage

The add-on maps extracted fields to the following CIM data models:

  • Network Traffic – Source and destination addresses, ports, protocols, bytes transferred
  • Web – URLs, HTTP methods, status codes, user agents
  • Authentication – User identities, authentication outcomes, source systems
  • Intrusion Detection – Alert severity, signatures, attack categories
  • Network Sessions – Session duration, transport protocols, connection states
  • Change – Administrative changes and configuration modifications
  • Vulnerabilities – Detected vulnerabilities and associated CVE identifiers

Data Processing

The add-on expects Stormshield syslog events formatted in either LEGACY_LONG or RFC5424 format. Each incoming event is first classified by its base sourcetype (stormshield), then reclassified into a specific typed sourcetype based on the log type field embedded in the syslog message. Field extraction rules tailored to each log type parse the WELF (WebTrends Enhanced Log Format) key-value pairs and map them to CIM-compliant field names.

Deployment Architecture

The add-on ships without a default inputs.conf file. It provides only the knowledge objects necessary for sourcetype classification, field extraction, and CIM mapping. Administrators must create a local/inputs.conf file on the receiving Splunk instance to define the syslog listening port, destination index, and base sourcetype assignment.

api_v1.title: VMware Vision Ingestion Add-on
api_v1.description:

Install it on a heavy forwarder that parses raw VMware events, or on indexers when they are the first full parsing tier. Use the full VMware Vision app on search heads for field normalization, dashboards, data models and CIM mappings.

api_v1.documentation:
The add-on provides props.conf settings for:

  • vmware:vision:vcenter
  • vmware:vision:esxi
  • vmware:vision:aria
  • vmware:vision:json

Its active configuration is limited to the add-on definition and raw parsing settings. Deployment documentation and disabled examples are included for administrators to adapt. The package has no Python runtime dependency.

Install it where raw data is first fully parsed. If an HF has already parsed the VMware events, downstream indexers do not need another copy for that data path. If indexers parse the raw input, deploy the TA there; use the cluster manager for an indexer cluster.

Search-time VMware extraction remains the responsibility of the full app on the search head and its distributed-search knowledge bundle. Installing this TA alone does not produce normalized VM fields, populate CIM or repair a missing vmware_lookup.py on a search peer.

The TA does not configure a syslog receiver or VMware sender. Preserve the original event and source timestamp through your collection path. Changes to parsing settings affect newly ingested data; they do not repair framing or timestamps already indexed.

VMware Vision is an independent project and is not an official VMware, Broadcom or Splunk product.

api_v1.title: E2G Plant Asset Integrity Add-on
api_v1.license_name: Splunk End User License for Third Party Content
api_v1.description:
The E2G Plant Asset Integrity Add-on provides search-time CIM normalization and enrichment for authentication and audit data collected from the E2G Plant Asset Integrity application.

Authentication events are normalized and enriched for the Splunk Authentication data model, while audit and user activity events are normalized and enriched for the Splunk Change data model.

The add-on provides field mappings, derived fields, event types, tags, and search-time extractions to enrich E2G events and make supported data available to CIM-compatible searches, data models, and Splunk Enterprise Security content.

The default configuration supports index=e2g with sourcetypes e2g_authentication and E2G-Audit. Data collection is handled separately using Splunk DB Connect.
api_v1.documentation:
Supported Data

Authentication / Login

  • Database table: UserAccessLogEntry
  • Index: e2g
  • Sourcetype: e2g_authentication
  • CIM data model: Authentication

Audit / User Activity

  • Database table: TransactionLog
  • Index: e2g
  • Sourcetype: E2G-Audit
  • CIM data model: Change

Authentication

The add-on recognizes the following E2G authentication event types:

  • 0 - SuccessfulLogin
  • 1 - FailedLogin
  • 2 - UserLogout
  • 3 - ForcedLogout
  • 4 - Timeout

Successful and failed login events are mapped to the Authentication data model. Logout, forced logout, and timeout events remain searchable but are not tagged as authentication attempts.

Authentication normalization includes user, action, app, signature, and signature_id.

Audit

E2G audit records are normalized to the Change data model. UserName is mapped to user, DataItemWrapperOid to object and object_id, and Keyword values contained in AuditLogEntries are exposed through the multivalue object_attrs field.

The add-on does not assign a static action to audit events because a single TransactionLog record can contain multiple audit entries.

Data Collection

This add-on does not configure the database connection or DB Connect inputs. Authentication and audit records must first be collected from the E2G application database and indexed in Splunk.

api_v1.title: WALLIX Bastion Add-on
api_v1.description: Technology Add-on that parses, normalizes and CIM-maps WALLIX Bastion Privileged Access Management syslog events. Supports both WALLIX syslog dialects (modern RFC 5424 double-quoted key=\"value\" and legacy WAB(CORE) single-quoted key='value'). Search-time knowledge only: no scripts, no third-party libraries, no compiled binaries.
api_v1.documentation:
1. What it does

WALLIX Bastion emits one mixed syslog stream containing seven log families.
The add-on splits it into one sourcetype per family, extracts the fields, and
maps them onto the Splunk Common Information Model.

Two things vary independently, and all four combinations are handled. The
envelope is either RFC 5424 or RFC 3164 / BSD, with or without a priority. The
payload uses either double quotes or the legacy WAB(CORE) single quotes.
Production appliances commonly pair a BSD envelope with a double-quoted
payload.

envelope   RFC 5424   <14>1 2024-06-26T22:37:26+01:00 host app pid - -
           BSD        <14>Aug 28 12:26:45 host sshproxy[13656]:

payload    modern     key="value"
           legacy     key='value'      (WAB(CORE))
                          ┌─ [wabaudit] ──────────► wallix:bastion:audit      → Change
                          ├─ [wabauth] / WAB(CORE) ► wallix:bastion:auth       → Authentication
  Bastion syslog ─────────┼─ [SSH|RDP Session] ───► wallix:bastion:session    → Authentication
  (wallix:bastion)        │                                                      Network Traffic
                          │                                                      Endpoint/Processes
                          ├─ [sshproxy|rdpproxy] ─► wallix:bastion:proxy      → Network Traffic
                          ├─ [Vault Activity] ────► wallix:bastion:vault      → Change (credential)
                          ├─ [sessionintegrity] ──► wallix:bastion:integrity  → (vendor + eventtypes)
                          └─ pam_unix / sudo ─────► wallix:bastion:system     → (vendor + eventtypes)

2. Fields and CIM mapping

Vendor fields are prefixed wallix_, keeping the WALLIX key name verbatim
after the prefix: action="add" becomes wallix_action=add. CIM fields are
computed on top of them.

Data model Sourcetypes Tags
Authentication :auth, :session authentication, privileged, default
Change :audit, :vault change, account
Network Traffic :proxy, :session network, communicate, session, start, end
Endpoint / Processes :session (NEW_PROCESS, COMPLETED_PROCESS) process, report, endpoint

WALLIX writes durations as H:MM:SS; the add-on converts them to seconds in
the CIM duration field and keeps the original in wallix_duration.

vendor_product is set on every event, but it is not a field of the CIM
Authentication data model. There, authentication_service is the handle on
WALLIX events - it is wallix:bastion on both :auth and :session. The
directory that answered the authentication is kept in wallix_auth_domain and
mapped to src_nt_domain. Change, Network Traffic and Endpoint do carry
vendor_product.

A data model that stays empty while the raw search returns events is almost
always the CIM index scope. The README covers the fix: every cim_*_indexes
macro in Splunk_SA_CIM has to list your index.

In an estate with several appliances, wallix_syslog_host carries the name the
emitting Bastion put in its own syslog header. Splunk's host may say
something else entirely - the relay's address, or the collector's - depending
on how the stream reaches you.

Security-relevant eventtypes (no CIM tag - for correlation searches)

wallix_bastion_session_integrity_failure   a session recording failed its integrity check
wallix_bastion_forbidden_pattern           PATTERN_FOUND / KILL_PATTERN_DETECTED
wallix_bastion_clipboard_exfiltration      clipboard copied OUT of a target
wallix_bastion_file_transfer               SFTP / RDP drive redirection
wallix_bastion_keystrokes                  KBD_INPUT

3. Search macros

wallix_bastion            all events
wallix_bastion_auth       primary authentication
wallix_bastion_audit      administration audit trail
wallix_bastion_sessions   privileged session activity
wallix_bastion_vault      credential checkout / checkin
wallix_bastion_index      index selector - override this one in local/

Examples:

| tstats count from datamodel=Authentication
  where Authentication.authentication_service="wallix:bastion"
        Authentication.action=failure
  by Authentication.user, Authentication.src

`wallix_bastion_sessions` wallix_type=CB_COPYING_PASTING_DATA_FROM_REMOTE_SESSION*
| stats count by src_user, user, dest, wallix_service

`wallix_bastion_audit` wallix_action=delete wallix_object_type=User
| table _time, user, src, object, object_attrs

5. Coming from TA-WALLIX_Bastion 1.0.x

Every WB_* field of the archived WALLIX add-on https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/3661 is provided as a FIELDALIAS,
and the legacy WB:syslog sourcetype is still recognised, so both add-ons can
run side by side. To get the CIM mapping, re-point your inputs to
sourcetype = wallix:bastion.

6. Companion app

SA-wallix-advanced-monitoring builds on this add-on: four Dashboard Studio
views over privileged access, session content, the administration audit trail
and the security signals, plus nine detections that ship unscheduled, so you
can run each one by hand and judge its threshold before enabling it. Like this
one it is pure configuration - no Python, no binaries.

api_v1.title: DECTRAX Add-on for Splunk
api_v1.description: Ingests and normalizes DECTRAX autonomous deception events, honeytokens, and line-rate firewall interdictions into Splunk Common Information Model (CIM 5.0) Intrusion_Detection and Alerts data models with mathematically zero false positives.
api_v1.documentation:
The **DECTRAX Add-on for Splunk** (`TA-dectrax`) brings line-rate active deception telemetry and autonomous firewall containment into Splunk Enterprise and Splunk Enterprise Security (ES).

### Why DECTRAX?

Traditional detection relies on noisy heuristics, behavioral thresholds, and unbillable SIEM rule tuning. In contrast, DECTRAX deploys zero-agent internal decoy endpoints, synthetic credentials (honeytokens), and protocol traps (RDP, LDAP, SMB, Kerberos, SCADA/Modbus).

Because decoys carry zero production business traffic, any interaction represents confirmed adversary reconnaissance. `TA-dectrax` normalizes this high-fidelity signal at line rate and accelerates incident response playbooks.

### Core Capabilities:

1. **Common Information Model (CIM 5.0) Compliant**: Automatically maps events to `Intrusion_Detection` and `Alerts` data models in Splunk Enterprise Security.

2. **Dual-Ingestion Architecture**:

- **HTTP Event Collector (HEC)**: Stream high-volume JSON telemetry directly from DECTRAX Cloud or On-Premises API Gateways (`sourcetype\="dectrax:json"`).

- **High-Throughput Syslog**: Ingest RFC-5424 structured syslog (`\<130>1 ... [dectrax@5424 ...]`) and ArcSight CEF 0.1 logs from on-premise VPS deception agents (`sourcetype\="dectrax:syslog"`).

3. **Automated Firewall Interdiction Tracking**: Captures sub-1.5s Palo Alto / Fortinet / Linux nftables External Dynamic List (EDL) IP drop actions directly in Splunk.

4. **Analyst & Executive Dashboard**: Out-of-the-box dark-mode dashboard showing 24h breach volume, trapped adversary IPs, targeted ports, and MITRE ATT\&CK techniques.

api_v1.description:
The Scaleway Add-On for Splunk enables seamless integration between Scaleway Audit Trail and Splunk Enterprise/Cloud platforms. This technology add-on (TA) serves as the data collection layer, allowing Splunk administrators to securely ingest audit logs from Scaleway infrastructure into their Splunk deployment.
The add-on addresses the critical need for centralized security monitoring and compliance reporting by providing a reliable, configurable bridge between Scaleway’s Audit Trail service and Splunk’s powerful analytics capabilities.
It handles authentication, data retrieval, and log forwarding while maintaining security best practices through encrypted connection and credential management.

Key Capabilities :
- Secure authentication with Scaleway accounts via API credentials
- Configurable audit log collection with filtering options
- Support for multiple Scaleway organizations and projects
- Automated log ingestion with configurable polling intervals
- CIM-compatible field extractions for seamless integration with Splunk apps
- Optimized data collection for Scaleway Audit Trail events

This add-on is designed for security teams, DevOps engineers, and compliance
officers who need to monitor Scaleway infrastructure activity, detect anomalies,
and maintain audit trails for regulatory compliance.

The Scaleway Add-On works in conjunction with the Scaleway App for Splunk
(frontend visualization app) to provide end-to-end security monitoring and
reporting capabilities.
api_v1.documentation:
The Scaleway Add-On for Splunk provides comprehensive audit log collection

from Scaleway cloud infrastructure. Once configured, the add-on continuously

polls Scaleway Audit Trail APIs and forwards events to Splunk for indexing

and analysis.

What this add-on collects:

- All audit events from Scaleway Audit Trail service

- IAM logs about users, groups, and applications

Use cases:

- Security incident investigation and forensics

- Compliance auditing and reporting

- User activity monitoring and access governance

- Change tracking and configuration management

- Anomaly detection and threat hunting

- Operational troubleshooting and root cause analysis

Integration:

This add-on produces CIM-compatible events that work seamlessly with:

- Splunk Enterprise Security (ES)

- Splunk IT Service Intelligence (ITSI)

- Custom dashboards and correlation searches

Requirements:

- Active Scaleway account

- API credentials with appropriate permissions

- Splunk versions currently supported: 9.4.x, 10.0.x, 10.2.x, and 10.4.x

api_v1.title: BXTI Add-on for Global Relay
api_v1.license_name: Splunk End User License for Third Party Content
api_v1.description: BXTI Add-on for Global Relay collects audit and activity events from the Global Relay Event Log API and indexes them in Splunk using the globalrelay:eventlog sourcetype. It provides secure credential management, configurable collection intervals, continuation checkpointing, JSON field extraction, and initial CIM mappings for authentication, data access, and change activity.
api_v1.documentation:
BXTI Add-on for Global Relay provides a configurable modular input for collecting audit and activity data from the Global Relay Event Log API.

Features

• Collects Global Relay Event Log API events over HTTPS.

• Stores API credentials using Splunk's encrypted credential storage.

• Supports customer-provisioned and regional Event Log API endpoints.

• Provides a configurable polling interval with a minimum interval of 6 seconds and a recommended interval of 15 seconds or greater.

• Uses the API continuation URL as a checkpoint so collection can resume without restarting from the beginning.

• Writes each API record as an individual JSON event.

• Assigns the globalrelay:eventlog sourcetype.

• Extracts JSON fields automatically.

• Provides event types and tags for initial CIM alignment with Authentication, Data Access, and Change activity.

• Includes the globalrelay_index search macro so administrators can define the appropriate search scope for their environment.

Data source

The add-on collects events available to the configured Global Relay Event Log API account. Available EventType values and event contents depend on the services, permissions, and audit activity enabled in the customer's Global Relay environment.

Example search

`globalrelay_index`

To inspect event types:

`globalrelay_index`

| stats count by EventType

| sort - count

To review CIM classifications:

`globalrelay_index`

| stats count by tag, EventType

Configuration

After installation, open BXTI Add-on for Global Relay in Splunk Web. Configure a Global Relay account, and then create an input using the API endpoint supplied for your organization. Select the destination index and an appropriate collection interval.

This add-on is independently developed by BXTI Splunk Team and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Global Relay.

api_v1.title: Rubric Protocol Add-on for Splunk
api_v1.description: Rubric Protocol produces court-grade evidence of AI system activity: every AI decision is signed with ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) post-quantum cryptography and anchored to Hedera Consensus Service, making it independently verifiable years later — without trusting application logs. This add-on parses Rubric attestation events delivered via HTTP Event Collector so SOC and GRC teams can monitor AI activity alongside the rest of their telemetry: which agents acted, what was attested, which federation node handled it, and whether each attestation is anchored. Every event carries a one-click verify_url to Rubric's public verifier for independent confirmation. Built for teams facing AI audit and compliance requirements (EU AI Act, SR 26-2, Illinois SB 315) who need AI activity visible in Splunk today.
api_v1.documentation:
This add-on contains search-time knowledge objects only — no scripts, no inputs, no stored credentials.

Sourcetypes:

- rubric:attestation — JSON events (default emitter format), parsed with KV_MODE\=json

- rubric:cef — CEF:0 events (RubricProtocol|RubricProof), parsed with dedicated field extractions

Extracted fields (CEF): attestation_id, hcs_topic, hcs_sequence, tier, sig_alg, agent_id, payload_hash, federation_node, action_path, plus a computed verify_url pointing at Rubric's public verifier (rubric-protocol.com/verify) for one-click independent verification of any event.

An eventtype (rubric_attestation_anchored) covers both sourcetypes for easy searching and alerting.

Example searches:

- All AI attestations in the last hour: eventtype\=rubric_attestation_anchored earliest\=-1h

- Attestations by agent: sourcetype\=rubric:cef | stats count by agent_id

- Unanchored backlog check: sourcetype\=rubric:cef NOT hcs_sequence\=* | stats count

About Rubric Protocol: rubric-protocol.com

api_v1.title: NetKit Add-on
api_v1.description:
The NetKit Add-on collects network probe telemetry and emits it as JSON events: TCP connect latency, internet throughput, DNS resolution, and TLS certificate health.

Four scheduled modular inputs write the sourcetypes netkit:ping, netkit:speedtest, netkit:dns, and netkit:tls, with probe execution logs captured to _internal as netkit_log. Targets, resolvers, schedules, and private CAs are managed from the add-on's Splunk Web UI.

The add-on runs on a full Splunk Enterprise instance (heavy forwarder, standalone, or search head). Universal Forwarders cannot run these inputs. Install the companion NetKit App on your search heads for dashboards, field extraction, and CIM normalization.
api_v1.documentation:
Overview

The NetKit Add-on runs scheduled network probes directly on a full Splunk
Enterprise instance and emits structured JSON telemetry for TCP connection
health, internet bandwidth, DNS resolution, and TLS certificate validation. It
is the collection half of NetKit; the companion
NetKit App ships the dashboards,
field extraction, and CIM normalization.

Probes

Ping

Measures TCP connect latency by timing the handshake to each configured
host:port target. This is not ICMP echo; it measures the time to establish a
TCP socket. Each run records connection success or failure, latency in
milliseconds, and the target details, over IPv4 and IPv6.

Speedtest

Measures internet throughput against Cloudflare's speed measurement endpoints
at speed.cloudflare.com, recording download and upload throughput in Mbps,
latency, and test duration. Selectable bandwidth profiles (low, standard, high,
or custom) control how much data each run transfers. All connections use HTTPS
with TLS certificate verification enforced.

DNS

Resolves configured domains and record types against the system resolvers or a
custom resolver list, falling back to TCP automatically when a reply is
truncated. Each lookup records the answers returned, the reply code, and
resolution latency. Domains are managed as reusable named groups.

TLS certificate inspection

Connects to each configured host:port target, retrieves the presented
certificate, and verifies it against the bundled certifi CA list or a private
CA you upload. Each inspection records:

  • Certificate subject and issuer distinguished names
  • Validity period (not-before and not-after)
  • Verification result, plus negotiated TLS version and cipher
  • Public key type and size, extended key usage OIDs, key usage, and signature
    algorithm
  • Chain length, where the bundled Python exposes the verified chain

Data collection

Sourcetype Contents
netkit:ping TCP connect latency results
netkit:speedtest Throughput and latency measurements
netkit:dns DNS lookup results
netkit:tls Certificate inspection results
netkit_log Probe execution logs, written to _internal

Probe events are JSON. Following Splunk's schema-on-read model, probes emit raw
canonical values (OIDs, integers, booleans, measurements) and the NetKit App
applies all naming and labeling at search time, so display changes never
require a new add-on release.

The add-on ships no indexes.conf. Create your destination index and select it
on each input; the NetKit App's netkit_index macro points searches at it.

Configuration

Inputs and settings are managed from the add-on's UI in Splunk Web:

  • Inputs: create Ping, Speedtest, DNS lookup, and TLS certificate
    inspection inputs, each with its own targets, interval, and index.
  • Configuration: Logging level, global Settings, Domains (named domain
    groups for DNS lookups), DNS Resolvers, and Certificate Authorities for
    uploading a private CA used to verify internal TLS targets.

Requirements

The add-on must run on a full Splunk Enterprise instance: heavy forwarder,
standalone, or search head. Universal Forwarders lack the Python runtime the
modular inputs need. Splunk Cloud is not a deployment target for the add-on,
since Cloud does not run these inputs; collect on-premises and forward to your
indexing tier. Only the NetKit App is installed on Splunk Cloud search heads.

Probes run as modular inputs on Splunk's bundled Python interpreter. The
add-on vendors no third-party packages of its own, using the standard library
plus libraries Splunk already ships, and never shells out to external ping or
speedtest binaries.

apps.csv_name: Inno S3 Streaming Add-on for AWS S3

api_v1.title: Inno S3 Streaming Add-on for AWS S3
api_v1.description: Serverless S3→Splunk ingestion over HEC, deployed from the Splunk UI. Event-driven and high-throughput — scales past 100 TB/day, searchable in minutes. Free.
api_v1.documentation:
What it does
This add-on lets a Splunk administrator deploy a serverless AWS Lambda into their own AWS account — entirely from the Splunk UI, using the AWS API (no console, no CLI). The Lambda streams S3 objects into Splunk over HEC on S3 ObjectCreated, so data is typically searchable within a minute of landing in S3. Ingestion is event-driven (no polling), scales with Lambda concurrency, and back to zero when idle.

Key features

  • One-click deploy from the Search Head. Fill in a short form and click Deploy — the add-on provisions the Lambda, its IAM role, and the S3 event trigger via the AWS API.
  • Runs entirely in your AWS account. Data flows S3 → Lambda → your HEC directly. Nothing passes through the vendor.
  • AWS keys are never retained. Credentials are used only at deploy time and are auto-wiped after a successful deploy; the Lambda runs on its own least-privilege IAM role.
  • Automatic format detection. Compression (gzip / zstd / bzip2 / uncompressed) is detected by magic bytes, not file extension. Layout is auto-detected: NDJSON (one event per line), whole-file JSON — a {"Records":[…]} envelope or bare array (one event per element, constant memory) — and plain-text lines.
  • Automatic AWS log source-typing (on by default). When no routing rule matches, the Lambda recognizes well-known AWS log S3 key paths and assigns the matching source type: CloudTrail → aws:cloudtrail, VPC Flow → aws:cloudwatchlogs:vpcflow (header line skipped), ELB/ALB → aws:elb:accesslogs, Config → aws:config, WAF → aws:waf. Your index is unchanged, and it can be turned off.
  • Per-prefix routing. Map any S3 key prefix to a specific index and source type (longest prefix wins); routes always override auto-detection and are validated at deploy time. Optionally post to HEC /raw and skip a header line.
  • Air-gap ready. Corporate-proxy support and an exportable, self-contained deploy script for environments where Splunk has no outbound AWS access.

For full field extraction of the AWS source types above, install the Splunk Add-on for AWS on your search tier — this add-on assigns the correct source type; the Splunk Add-on for AWS provides the parsing.

Compatibility

  • Splunk Cloud Platform (Victoria Experience) and Splunk Enterprise (9.x and later), Python 3.
  • Passes Splunk AppInspect cloud checks.

Free — no license key and no subscription. You pay AWS directly for the Lambda compute you use.

apps.csv_name: Cloudflare R2 Log Ingestion Add-on for Splunk

api_v1.title: Cloudflare R2 Log Ingestion Add-on for Splunk
api_v1.description:
Cloudflare R2 Log Ingestion is a Splunk Technology Add-on (TA) that pulls Cloudflare
Logpush log files directly from a Cloudflare R2 bucket into Splunk, using a
purpose-built modular input that speaks R2's S3-compatible API.

Key capabilities:
- Works with any Cloudflare Logpush dataset (Gateway DNS, HTTP Requests, Access, Audit, and more) - fully dataset-agnostic
- One input per bucket/prefix, each with its own sourcetype and index, so a single Splunk instance can ingest multiple Logpush datasets side by side
- Credentials live in a reusable, encrypted Account (stored via Splunk's storage/passwords, never in inputs.conf); any number of Cloudflare accounts can feed the same Splunk instance
- Checkpointing via a typed KV Store processed-key set plus a configurable lookback window, so restarts don't lose progress and late-delivered Logpush batches are still picked up (not a single fragile monotonic cursor)
- The R2 access layer is pure Python standard library - no boto3, no botocore, no vendored AWS SDK to keep patched

Pairs well with the Cloudflare App for Splunk for dashboards and field extractions
once the data is in Splunk.

Requirements: Splunk Enterprise 9.4 or higher. Requires KV Store, so it runs on a
heavy forwarder, IDM, standalone, or search head - not a Universal Forwarder. This
release targets on-premises Splunk Enterprise only; Splunk Cloud is not currently a
supported deployment target.
api_v1.documentation:
Architecture

  • bin/cloudflare_r2_helper.py - the modular input: resolves the Account's credentials via solnlib, lists new R2 objects (deduped against a KV Store processed-key set plus lookback window), streams and decompresses each object,
    and checkpoints after each object's events are emitted.
  • bin/r2client.py - a standalone R2 client with zero third-party dependencies: SigV4 signing via hmac/hashlib, HTTPS via urllib.request over stdlib ssl,
    ListObjectsV2 XML parsing via xml.etree, and streaming gzip decompression.

Checkpointing design

Progress is tracked as a typed KV Store collection (one row per ingested object),
not a single cursor. Logpush filenames are timestamped by the log time window, not
by delivery time, and Logpush can retry delivery - a single monotonic cursor would
permanently skip a late-delivered batch whose key sorts before the cursor. Re-listing
the configured lookback window and deduping per object avoids that. Delivery is
at-least-once: a checkpoint is written only after its events are emitted, so an
ungraceful crash mid-object may re-ingest that object on the next poll (a small
number of duplicate events). Under normal operation, each object is ingested exactly
once with no search-time deduplication required.

Credential security

Credentials live in a Splunk UCC Account whose secret field is encrypted; Splunk
routes it to storage/passwords at save time, and the input reads it back via
solnlib at runtime. No plaintext credential is ever written to a Splunk conf file.

Third-party licensing

The R2 client itself has no third-party runtime dependencies. The Splunk-supplied
UCC toolchain libraries bundled at build time (splunklib, solnlib, splunktaucclib,
and their transitive dependencies - 14 packages total, all permissively licensed:
Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD, BSD-3-Clause, MPL-2.0, PSF-2.0) are fully disclosed with their
license texts in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt inside the package.

apps.csv_name: Qualys Universal Technology Add-on (TA) for Splunk

api_v1.title: Qualys Universal Technology Add-on (TA) for Splunk
api_v1.license_name: Splunk End User License for Third Party Content
api_v1.description: The Qualys Universal Technology Add-on (TA) for Splunk enables organizations to collect Qualys VMDR (Vulnerability Management Detection and Response) and Qualys WAS (Web Application Scanning) data and ingest it into Splunk for monitoring, analysis, reporting, and investigation. Built on the Splunk Universal Configuration Console (UCC) framework, this add-on delivers a modern configuration experience with asynchronous data collection, multi-account support, KV Store checkpointing for resumable collection, and compatibility with Splunk versions supporting Python 3.9+. This is a separate add-on from the existing Qualys Technology Add-on (TA) for Splunk (App ID 2964). This Universal TA currently supports Qualys VMDR and Qualys WAS modules.
api_v1.documentation:
Architecture

The add-on uses Splunk modular inputs to connect to Qualys REST APIs over HTTPS. Data flows through module-specific collectors (VMDR Collector, WAS Collector) that process API responses asynchronously. Collected data is normalized, transformed, and enriched before being indexed into Splunk. Collection progress is tracked using KV Store checkpoints, enabling reliable, resumable data collection across restarts and interruptions.

Prerequisites

Qualys Requirements:

  • Active Qualys subscription
  • Valid Qualys API credentials
  • Module access permissions for VMDR and/or WAS

Splunk Requirements:

  • Supported Splunk Enterprise deployment
  • Administrative privileges on the Splunk instance
  • KV Store enabled and operational
  • Python 3.9+ support

Network Requirements:

  • HTTPS connectivity to Qualys API endpoints
  • Proxy configuration (if required by your environment)
  • Access to Splunk management services

System Requirements:

  • Linux operating system

Getting Started

  1. Download and install the add-on on your Splunk instance.
  2. Open the add-on configuration page and add your Qualys account credentials.
  3. Configure data inputs for the Qualys modules you want to collect (VMDR, WAS).
  4. Optionally configure proxy settings and logging levels.
  5. Begin searching and reporting on your Qualys data in Splunk.
Support and Resources

For documentation please see: https://docs.qualys.com/en/integration/splunk-ucc/get_started/get_started.htm

Support

In case any assistance is needed, please visit https://success.qualys.com/customersupport/s/

api_v1.title: TekStream Add-on for Keri Borealis
api_v1.license_name: Splunk End User License for Third Party Content
api_v1.description: The Keri Borealis Add-on for Splunk collects live door access and badge reader events from the Keri Borealis access control platform through its API. The add-on retrieves controller, trunk, source, credential, and event detail data from Borealis systems and provides field extractions to normalize access control events in Splunk. It supports configurable polling intervals and historical data collection, enabling security teams to monitor physical access events and investigate badge reader activity across Borealis-managed facilities. The add-on includes two dashboards for managing configuration settings and monitoring data inputs, and it uses KV store-based checkpointing to track collection state and prevent data loss during interruptions.
api_v1.documentation:
Overview

The Keri Borealis Add-on for Splunk integrates with the Keri Borealis access control platform to collect physical security events in real time. The add-on connects to the Borealis API to retrieve door access logs, badge reader events, and related access control data, making this information available for security monitoring, compliance reporting, and incident investigation within Splunk.

Data Collection

The add-on collects events from the following data sources:

  • keri_aetheros_borealis: Primary data source for Borealis access control events

Collected data is indexed with the source types borealis and the logs for the TA's modular input are tagged with takeriborealis:log.

Field Extractions

The add-on provides field extractions for key access control attributes:

  • Controller information: Identifies the specific access control hardware unit generating events
  • Trunk data: Captures the communication pathway and network segment details
  • Source identification: Tracks the origin point of access attempts
  • Credential details: Extracts badge, card, or other credential identifiers used in access events
  • Event metadata: Provides timestamps, event types, and access decision outcomes

These extractions enable filtering, correlation, and analysis of physical access patterns across Borealis-managed facilities.

Dashboards

The add-on includes two built-in dashboards:

  • Configuration Dashboard: Provides interface for managing add-on settings and API parameters
  • Inputs Dashboard: Displays active data inputs and their collection status

API Integration

The add-on connects to the Keri API endpoint to retrieve access control events. Administrators configure the credentials (Client ID and Secret Key), base URL, tenant name, and site name to establish the connection. The add-on supports configurable polling intervals and page sizes to balance collection frequency with API load. Historical data collection is available by setting a timestamp_start parameter to define the initial collection point.

Checkpoint Management

The add-on uses Splunk's KV store to maintain collection checkpoints. The TA_keri_borealis_checkpointer collection tracks the last successfully retrieved event for each input, ensuring data continuity during restarts or network interruptions. This checkpoint mechanism prevents duplicate event collection and enables reliable recovery from temporary failures.

apps.csv_name: DarkStrata Threat Intelligence Add-on for Splunk

api_v1.title: DarkStrata Threat Intelligence Add-on for Splunk
api_v1.license_name: Splunk End User License for Third Party Content
api_v1.description:
DarkStrata Threat Intelligence Add-on for Splunk brings DarkStrata's credential-exposure intelligence directly into Splunk and Splunk Enterprise Security (ES), so your SOC can detect and respond to compromised credentials before they're used against you.

DarkStrata continuously monitors breach data, infostealer/malware logs and third-party exposure for credentials tied to your organisation. This add-on pulls that intelligence into Splunk as structured, CIM-compliant events - ready for correlation, alerting, dashboards and automated response.

Use it to:

- Detect compromised credentials before they're used maliciously
- Identify malware infections through infostealer credential detection
- Monitor third-party risk by tracking corporate credentials exposed on external sites
- Automate incident response via ES notable events, correlation searches and adaptive-response actions
- Enrich threat hunting with credential-exposure context

Data is delivered in STIX 2.1 format and mapped to the Authentication and Threat Intelligence CIM data models, so it works out of the box with Enterprise Security's threat-intelligence framework. Collection is incremental and checkpoint-based - only new intelligence is fetched on each run - with configurable batching, rate limiting and connection pooling for predictable performance.
api_v1.documentation:
Data collection

  • Two modular inputs: Indicators (/stix/indicators) and Alerts (/stix/alerts)
  • Checkpoint-based incremental sync (KV Store)
  • API credentials validated on save; optional proxy support (HTTP/SOCKS5)

Data model & knowledge objects

  • Sourcetypes: darkstrata:stix:observed-data, darkstrata:stix:alert
  • CIM mappings for Authentication and Threat Intelligence
  • Pre-built event types, tags, macros and lookups

Enterprise Security integration

  • Threat-intelligence KV Store collections
  • Pre-built correlation searches for notable events
  • Adaptive-response actions: update alert status, close alert, reopen alert, and get alert details (enrichment)

Automation & privacy

  • Sample Splunk SOAR playbooks (credential-exposure triage, auto-acknowledge, alert enrichment)
  • Optional SHA-256 email hashing for privacy/compliance
  • Confidence-score filtering (maps STIX confidence to threat severity)

apps.csv_name: DataRunk Add-on for Barracuda Email Gateway Defense

api_v1.title: DataRunk Add-on for Barracuda Email Gateway Defense
api_v1.description:
Barracuda Email Gateway Defense (EGD) is a comprehensive Splunk application designed to collect, parse, and visualize security events from Barracuda Email Gateway Defense appliances. This app enables organizations to centralize email security monitoring, threat analysis, and compliance reporting through real-time dashboards and detailed analytics.
The app addresses critical email security challenges:
- Email Threat Detection: Monitor malware, spam, and phishing attempts in real-time
- Security Incident Investigation: Track email routing, authentication failures, and policy violations
- Compliance & Audit: Generate compliance reports for security policies and data retention
- Security Posture Analysis: Identify trends, top threats, and vulnerable users
Key Features:
• Pre-built dashboards for threat analysis and executive overview
• CIM-compliant data models for efficient searching
• Support for both Splunk Enterprise and Splunk Cloud
• Automatic data parsing with indexed fields for rapid investigation
• Out-of-the-box visualizations and saved searches
api_v1.documentation:
OVERVIEW
The Barracuda Email Gateway Defense app transforms raw email security logs into actionable intelligence. It provides security teams with immediate visibility into email threats, user behavior patterns, and security policy compliance.
MAIN DASHBOARDS & FEATURES
Executive Overview
- Threat summary and KPIs
- Top attack types and blocked senders
- User activity heatmap
- Incident timeline
Threat Analysis
- Malware and phishing detection breakdown
- Attack vectors and techniques
- Threat actor profiling
- Suspicious sender analysis
User & Endpoint Security
- User risk assessment
- Compromised account detection
- Email forwarding patterns
- Suspicious recipient analysis
Email Flow & Authentication
- Email routing analysis
- Authentication failure tracking
- SPF/DKIM/DMARC compliance
- TLS encryption status
Compliance & Audit
- Policy violation reports
- Data retention tracking
- Audit trail analytics

DATA SOURCES
- Barracuda Email Gateway Defense appliance (syslog/JSON format)

- Supports both on-premises and cloud-based deployments
CIM COMPLIANCE
This app is CIM (Common Information Model) compliant, enabling:
- Seamless integration with other security apps
- Standardized field mappings
- Enhanced search capabilities across data models
LOOKUP TABLES

- Action Mapping: Email action normalization (allow, block, quarantine, etc.)
- Audit Action Tracking: Detailed action audit trails

api_v1.title: Mars Alert Forwarding Add-on
api_v1.description:
Mars Alert Forwarding adds a "Send to Mars" custom alert action that forwards a triggered saved search's results directly to the Mars Security platform in a single outbound delivery.

The problem it solves: security teams using Mars for AI-driven threat hunting and detection engineering need their Splunk detections to flow into Mars without manual exporting, copy-pasting results, or building and maintaining custom webhook scripts. This add-on bridges that gap with a simple, native alert action.

How it works:
- Add "Send to Mars" to any saved search under Trigger Actions. When the alert fires, the add-on sends the matching results, the SPL behind the search, the configured severity, and key search metadata to your Mars webhook.

- Splunk severity (1–5) is mapped to Mars severity automatically, with an optional per-action override.
Setup is a one-time admin task: open the add-on's setup page and enter your Mars webhook URL and token (stored encrypted in Splunk), then enable the action on any saved search.

Note: this add-on forwards data to the Mars platform and requires a Mars account.

api_v1.title: Postfix Mail Add-on for Splunk
api_v1.description:
The Postfix Mail Add-on for Splunk helps administrators, mail system engineers, and SOC teams parse, normalize, and analyze Postfix mail server logs in Splunk.
The add-on provides search-time field extractions, field aliases, event types, tags, and CIM-aligned mappings for common Postfix mail events. It is designed for Postfix logs collected from /var/log/maillog or equivalent syslog files using the recommended sourcetype postfix:syslog.
api_v1.documentation:
The Postfix Mail Add-on for Splunk provides parsing and normalization for Postfix mail server logs.

It is intended for environments where Postfix logs are collected into Splunk and need to be searched, analyzed, and mapped to normalized mail-related fields.

The add-on uses the recommended sourcetype:

`postfix:syslog`

api_v1.title: CMS Technical Add-on for Splunk
api_v1.description: The CMS Technical Add-on for Splunk integrates Cisco Meeting Server (CMS) data into Splunk by collecting and indexing call detail records (CDR) and media quality statistics transmitted via syslog. The add-on handles all aspects of data ingestion, including creating custom indexes for CDR data, media statistics, and general syslog events. It parses incoming XML-formatted CDR events and structured syslog messages into searchable fields. The add-on is designed for deployment on indexers and heavy forwarders where CMS data collection occurs. It provides the foundational data layer for CMS analytics but does not include visualization dashboards or user-facing interfaces beyond a setup page. Organizations using Cisco Meeting Server can leverage this add-on to capture detailed call metrics, media quality indicators, and operational logs for troubleshooting, capacity planning, and quality of service analysis.
api_v1.documentation:
Overview

The CMS Technical Add-on for Splunk provides data collection and indexing capabilities for Cisco Meeting Server environments. The add-on receives call detail records and media quality statistics from CMS via syslog, parses the incoming data, and routes events to dedicated indexes for efficient search and analysis.

Data Collection

The add-on handles two primary data streams from Cisco Meeting Server:

  • Call Detail Records (CDR): XML-formatted records capturing detailed information about each call, including participant details, call duration, connection quality, and session metadata
  • Media Quality Statistics: Structured syslog messages containing real-time and summary statistics about media quality, including packet loss, jitter, latency, and codec performance metrics

Additionally, the add-on collects general CMS syslog messages for operational monitoring and troubleshooting.

Source Types

The add-on defines the following source types:

  • cms:cdr_xml: Call detail records in XML format
  • cms:syslog: General CMS syslog messages and media quality statistics

Index Architecture

The add-on creates three dedicated indexes to organize CMS data:

  • ta_cisco_cms_cdr: Stores call detail records
  • ta_cisco_cms_media_stats: Stores media quality statistics events (USERMEDIASTATS and USERCONFIGSTATS)
  • ta_cisco_cms_syslog: Stores general CMS syslog messages

This separation enables efficient data retention policies and targeted searches based on the type of CMS telemetry being analyzed.

Event Processing

The add-on applies regex-based pattern matching to route media statistics events correctly. USERMEDIASTATS and USERCONFIGSTATS events are identified and directed to the media statistics index, while other syslog messages are routed to the general syslog index. Unmatched syslog events are dropped by design to reduce noise and storage overhead.

Setup Dashboard

A setup view is accessible through the Splunk web interface (Apps > Manage Apps > Set up) that provides configuration guidance for connecting CMS to the Splunk forwarder. This interface offers details on syslog port configuration and CDR sender setup.

Deployment Architecture

This add-on should be deployed on indexers in distributed Splunk environments. In architectures using heavy forwarders for data collection, the add-on must be installed on those heavy forwarders as well to ensure proper parsing and routing of CMS events. The add-on does not provide dashboards or visualizations; it serves as the data ingestion layer that other applications can build upon.

api_v1.title: WithSecure Elements Add-on
api_v1.description: The WithSecure Elements Add-on collects endpoint protection and detection data from the WithSecure Elements API. It ingests EPP Security Events and EDR Broad Context Detections through OAuth2-authenticated modular inputs, enabling centralized security event analysis in Splunk. The add-on maps collected events to CIM endpoint, malware, intrusion detection, and process tags, facilitating correlation with other security data sources. Two modular inputs handle data collection: withsecure_epp_input retrieves endpoint protection events, while withsecure_bcd_input collects EDR broad context detection incidents. Events are indexed under source types withsecure:epp:security_event, withsecure:epp:bcd_incident, and withsecure:epp:bcd_detection. The add-on includes a custom search command for retrieving specific detection details and provides a workflow action to fetch incident detections directly from the Splunk interface.
api_v1.documentation:
Overview

The WithSecure Elements Add-on integrates WithSecure's endpoint protection platform and EDR capabilities with Splunk through authenticated API collection. The add-on establishes OAuth2-authenticated connections to the WithSecure Elements API, retrieving security events and detection data for analysis, correlation, and alerting.

Data Collection

The add-on provides two modular inputs for data collection:

  • withsecure_epp_input: Collects endpoint protection platform security events from WithSecure Elements. Events are indexed with source type withsecure:epp:security_event.
  • withsecure_bcd_input: Collects EDR broad context detection incidents. Events are indexed with source types withsecure:epp:bcd_incident and withsecure:epp:bcd_detection.

Both inputs authenticate to the WithSecure Elements API using OAuth2 client credentials. The add-on maintains checkpoint state in KV Store to track collection progress and prevent duplicate event ingestion.

CIM Compliance

The add-on maps WithSecure Elements events to the following CIM data model tags:

  • Endpoint
  • Malware
  • Intrusion Detection
  • Process

This mapping enables correlation with other CIM-compliant data sources and supports standardized detection and investigation workflows.

Custom Search Command

The add-on includes the fetchdetections custom search command, which retrieves detailed detection information for a specific incident. The command requires a 36-character UUID format incident identifier and queries the WithSecure Elements API to return associated detection data.

Workflow Action

The withsecure_detections workflow action provides an interface to fetch incident detections on-demand from the Splunk UI. This action integrates with the withsecure_bcd_input configuration: when auto_fetch_detections is disabled, users can selectively retrieve detections for specific incidents through the workflow action rather than collecting all detections automatically.

Technical Requirements

The add-on requires Python 3.7 or higher for execution. KV Store must be enabled and accessible, as checkpoint persistence relies on KV Store collections to maintain collection state across restarts. The Splunk instance must have network connectivity to api.connect.withsecure.com for API communication.

apps.csv_name: Datavira Add-on for USOM Threat Intelligence

api_v1.title: Datavira Add-on for USOM Threat Intelligence
api_v1.description: The USOM Threat Intelligence add-on integrates the Turkish Cybersecurity Presidency's TR-CERT threat-intelligence API into Splunk. It polls the USOM REST API on a configurable schedule and produces five lookup tables containing indicators of compromise: IP addresses, IPv6 addresses, IPv6 networks, domains, and URLs. The add-on resolves USOM's short threat-classification codes to English titles using companion API endpoints. For environments running Splunk Enterprise Security 7.0 or later, the add-on includes optional threatlist:// inputs that push these lookups into ES's threat intelligence framework for automated correlation. The add-on emits operational logs and per-cycle statistics events to aid monitoring and troubleshooting. On Search Head Clusters, the modular input automatically runs only on the captain and replicates lookup tables to members via bundle replication.
api_v1.documentation:
Overview

The USOM Threat Intelligence add-on connects Splunk to the public threat-intelligence API operated by USOM (Turkey's TR-CERT, part of the Turkish Cybersecurity Presidency). USOM discontinued its legacy text-format IOC distribution on June 1, 2026; this add-on uses the current JSON REST API at https://siberguvenlik.gov.tr/api/.

Capabilities

Threat Intelligence Collection

The add-on fetches indicators of compromise from the USOM API and writes them to five Splunk lookup tables:

  • usom_ip_intel — IPv4 addresses
  • usom_ip6_intel — IPv6 addresses
  • usom_ip6net_intel — IPv6 network ranges
  • usom_domain_intel — domain names
  • usom_url_intel — URLs

Each lookup record includes the indicator value, threat classification, and metadata returned by the API. The add-on resolves USOM's short threat-classification codes to English titles using companion API endpoints.

Enterprise Security Integration

For organizations running Splunk Enterprise Security 7.0 or later, the add-on includes optional threatlist:// modular inputs (disabled by default) that push each lookup into the ES threat intelligence framework. Administrators can enable these inputs individually from the Setup page after verifying ES is installed on the same search head or cluster.

Operational Monitoring

The add-on logs all operational messages to $SPLUNK_HOME/var/log/splunk/ta_usom_cti.log and emits one statistics event per fetch cycle to a configurable Splunk index (default _internal, sourcetype usom_ti:stats). Statistics events include cycle duration, record counts, and API response codes.

Search Head Cluster Support

On Search Head Clusters, the modular input automatically detects cluster membership and runs only on the captain. Lookup tables are replicated to cluster members via standard SHC bundle replication. Non-captain members silently skip execution; administrators can verify correct operation by inspecting the operational log for SHC membership messages.

Data Sources

The add-on produces two sourcetypes:

  • ta_usom_cti:log — operational logs from the modular input
  • usom_ti:stats — per-cycle statistics events

Dashboards

The add-on ships with two dashboards:

  • USOM Monitoring — displays fetch-cycle statistics, API response times, IOC counts by type, and recent operational logs
  • Setup — configuration interface for the modular input, proxy settings, and Enterprise Security integration toggles

api_v1.title: Teamviewer Add-on for Splunk
api_v1.license_name: Splunk End User License for Third Party Content
api_v1.description: The TeamViewer Add-on for Splunk collects and parses TeamViewer log files from Windows endpoints, enabling monitoring and security analysis of remote access sessions. The add-on ingests log data from TeamViewer 15.x installations, including session logs, network connection reports, and audit data. It provides field extractions that map TeamViewer events to the Common Information Model (CIM), specifically the Authentication, Network Sessions, Network Traffic, and Data Access data models. The add-on defines two source types: teamviewer for general session and audit logs, and teamviewer:network for network connection details. By normalizing TeamViewer data into CIM-compliant fields, the add-on enables correlation with other security data sources and supports use cases such as remote access auditing, connection monitoring, and security investigations involving remote support sessions.
api_v1.documentation:
Overview

The TeamViewer Add-on for Splunk ingests log data from TeamViewer 15.x installations on Windows endpoints. It collects three primary log sources:

  • TeamViewer15_Logfile.log: General session logs and audit events (sourcetype: teamviewer)
  • TVNetwork.log: Network connection reports (sourcetype: teamviewer:network)
  • TeamViewer15_Hooks.log: Hook and integration events (sourcetype: teamviewer)

The add-on reads log files from the default TeamViewer installation directory on Windows: C:\Program Files\TeamViewer\.

Data Model Compliance

The add-on provides field extractions that map TeamViewer events to four CIM data models:

  • Authentication: Remote access authentication events
  • Network Sessions: Session establishment and termination
  • Network Traffic: Network connection details and traffic patterns
  • Data Access: Audit trails for remote access to systems

CIM-compliant field extractions enable correlation with other security data sources and support enterprise security monitoring workflows.

Recommended Index Configuration

The add-on is designed to use a dedicated index named teamviewer. Administrators should create this index on all indexers before deploying the add-on to ensure proper data routing and retention policies.

Use Cases

  • Monitor remote access patterns across the enterprise
  • Audit TeamViewer sessions for compliance and security investigations
  • Correlate remote access events with authentication logs from other sources
  • Track network connections initiated through TeamViewer clients
  • Generate alerts on suspicious remote access activity

Technical Requirements

The add-on requires Splunk Enterprise or Universal Forwarder version 8.2 or later. Monitored endpoints must be running TeamViewer 15.x on Windows. The add-on supports Python versions 3.7 through 3.13.

api_v1.title: Add-on for Sophos Central CEF
api_v1.license_name: Splunk End User License for Third Party Content
api_v1.description: Add-on for Sophos Central CEF is a technical add-on that parses Sophos Central security events delivered via CEF-formatted syslog to a Splunk Heavy Forwarder. The add-on provides comprehensive field extractions, automatic sub-sourcetype routing, and CIM v5 data model tagging for integration with Splunk Enterprise Security. It processes threat detections from Sophos Intercept X, investigation and case management events, firewall gateway logs, web control violations, device telemetry, update activity, and behavioral analysis events. The add-on performs index-time sub-sourcetype routing based on the CEF deviceEventClassId field, splitting incoming sophos:cef:central events into nine distinct sourcetypes: threat, investigation, firewall, webcontrol, device, update, corebehavioral, and coreclean. Field extractions include MITRE ATT&CK technique mappings extracted from Sophos threat intelligence, enabling correlation of detections with adversary tactics. CIM v5 compliance covers the Malware, Intrusion Detection, Incident Management, Network Traffic, and Web data models, providing normalized field mappings for use in Enterprise Security correlation searches, notable events, and threat intelligence workflows.

api_v1.title: Ensign Akamai Web Security Add-on
api_v1.license_name: Splunk End User License for Third Party Content
api_v1.description:
Ensign Akamai Web Security Add-on for Splunk

An enterprise-grade alternative to the official Akamai SIEM app, rebuilt by adopt Splunk UCC Framework.

WHY THIS ADD-ON?
The official Akamai app (refer to : https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/4310) uses legacy way for enabled the input (via Settings => Data Input) and several parsing is not key-value-pair based after coming ingested in Splunk, rather than using spath and makes easier for analyst to choose the fields, this add-ons are one to solve that. This add-on provides:
- Full UI-driven configuration based on your usual for inputs based on Add-ons (just directly configured under the add-ons like the other Splunk Supported Add-ons).
- Multi-account management with encrypted credential storage via Splunk's native password vault
- Multi-proxy support (HTTP, HTTPS, SOCKS4, SOCKS5) with per-input proxy assignment
- Offset-based checkpointing for reliable data continuity across restarts.
- Custom sourcetype override per input for seamless migration.
- Deployment Server compatible.

DATA SOURCE:
Captures security events from Akamai SIEM Integration API v1, supporting:
- App & API Protector
- Kona Site Defender
- Web Application Protector
- Client Reputation
- Bot Manager
- Account Protector

EVENT PROCESSING:
- URL-decodes all fields recursively
- Parses HTTP headers into structured key-value pairs
- Decodes base64-encoded attackData rule fields into structured objects
- Drops summary/offset metadata events (nullQueue)

Ref: https://techdocs.akamai.com/siem-integration/docs

Built by Ensign Infosecurity Indonesia.

api_v1.title: Add-on for TOPdesk
api_v1.description:
The Add-on for TOPdesk connects Splunk to the TOPdesk REST API in both directions. It collects TOPdesk incidents into Splunk on a schedule, with filters on status, priority, category, operator group and open-only incidents, so service desk data can be searched, correlated and dashboarded next to your other machine data. It also ships an alert action that creates a TOPdesk incident directly from any Splunk alert, with the caller, priority, category and branch taken from the alert.

Built with the Splunk Add-on Builder on the UCC framework, Apache 2.0 licensed, and compatible with Splunk Enterprise 9.x and 10.x and Splunk Cloud Platform. Product page and support: https://www.orangeinsight.io/topdesk-addon
api_v1.documentation:
What the add-on does

Collect incidents (modular input TOPdesk Incidents)

• Polls GET /tas/api/incidents on the interval you choose (default every 5 minutes, or a cron expression).

• Filters on status (first line, second line or all), priority (P1 to P7, multi-select), category, operator group, and optionally only non-completed incidents.

• Incremental: each input keeps its own checkpoint in the KV store and only fetches incidents created since the last run (the first run takes the last 24 hours). TOPdesk pagination is followed automatically.

• Every incident is indexed as one JSON event with sourcetype topdesk:incident, ready for spath, dashboards, SLA reporting and correlation with other data.

• Honours Splunk proxy settings and certificate verification; retries transient failures with back-off and stops immediately on authentication errors.

Create incidents (alert action Create TOPdesk incident)

• Add it as a trigger action to any alert, or run it ad hoc with | sendalert create_topdesk_incident.

• Fields: brief description, request text, caller e-mail (looked up in TOPdesk), status (first or second line), priority, branch/site and category. $result.field$ tokens are supported, so the ticket carries the alert data.

• Input is validated before anything is sent; only transient HTTP errors are retried.

Security

• One configuration page: TOPdesk base URL, API user and application password. The password is stored encrypted in Splunk's credential store; authentication is HTTP Basic over HTTPS.

• Secrets never appear in the logs and caller e-mail addresses are masked.

Monitoring

• Every run and every alert execution writes log lines with a run id and request id to index\=_internal sourcetype\=addonfortopdesk:log, so a run can be followed end to end.

• Each run ends with one JSON MONITOR summary line (result: success, failed, auth_error, ...), suitable for health dashboards. A Monitoring dashboard with recent errors and warnings is included.

Requirements

• Splunk Enterprise 9.x or 10.x, or Splunk Cloud Platform (Python 3.9 or 3.13 runtime).

• A TOPdesk operator account with an application password: read rights on incidents for collection, create rights for the alert action.

• KV store enabled on the instance that runs the input.

Product page and support: https://www.orangeinsight.io/topdesk-addon

TOPdesk is a registered trademark of TOPdesk B.V. This app is not affiliated with or endorsed by TOPdesk.

api_v1.title: Ransomware Add-on for Splunk
api_v1.description: The Ransomware Add-on for Splunk integrates ransomware-related threat intelligence and incident data into your Splunk environment. This add-on leverages Python scripts to collect, parse, and organize data such as victim details, indicators of compromise (IOCs), ransomware notes, negotiation information, and YARA rules. It provides enhanced visibility into ransomware activities and enables efficient monitoring, alerting, and analysis within your Splunk ecosystem
api_v1.documentation:
Inputs Details
The add-on provides multiple Python-based scripts to extract and organize ransomware-related data. Key input modules include:
• Victim: Collects details about victims, including IP, hostname, and affected assets.
• CSIRT: Captures and processes Computer Security Incident Response Team reports.
• ListSectors: Organizes ransomware activity or victims into sectors/categories for analysis.
• Group Details: Manages groups associated with ransomware incidents.
• Group IOCs : Collects and processes indicators of compromise.
• Negotiation : Tracks ransomware negotiation logs.
